Senses.Explanation: Literally, to face a wall. The expression occurs 1,857 times in 308 allowlisted texts, and the Chan record makes it a named action rather than a general description of where someone sits. Bodhidharma's biography says that he sat facing the wall at Shaolin, remained silent throughout the day, and was called the wall-gazing brahman; the nine-year formula occurs 435 times in 150 texts. The action is not confined to Bodhidharma: the records say that Luzu faced the wall whenever a monk came, and later masters repeatedly ask why he did so. A verse on Luzu calls it the most effortless complete command, but immediately says that one who knows mind does not depend on a raised eyebrow to recognize another. Other masters criticize the inherited scenes: one calls Bodhidharma's nine years facing the wall a source of ghosts, while a verse collection preserves both praise and mockery around the same act. The corpus therefore records facing the wall as an action of masters, a recurring public-interview question, and an object of later criticism; it does not supply a single explanatory gloss for the act.
Senses.Note: One physical action covers Bodhidharma's sitting and Luzu's turning away from visitors; later praise, criticism, and questions are different readings of that same action, not separate senses under depth-gate item 8.

Occurrences.Kwic: 寓止于嵩山少林寺。面壁而坐。終日默然。人莫之測。謂之壁觀婆羅門。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 五燈會元: complete-case exact-turn review identifies Bodhidharma as the actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 米胡領眾來。纔欲相見。師便拽轉禪牀。面壁而坐。米於背後立。少時却回客位。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Datong Ji section. Datong Ji is the exact actor who turns the Chan seat and faces the wall when Mihu arrives; Mihu stands behind him and later returns to the guest place.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師頌魯祖面壁曰。魯祖三昧最省力。纔見僧來便面壁。若是知心達道人。不在揚眉便相悉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Transmission of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), Liangshan Shanji entry. Liangshan Shanji is the exact verse author who verses Luzu's wall-facing and describes Luzu facing the wall whenever a monk comes; Luzu is the subject of the verse, not the author of this headword-bearing verse turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 室中問僧：魯祖當日見僧來參，何故便面壁？眾下語不契，
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jiatai Universal Lamp Record (嘉泰普燈錄), Cuiyan Kezhen entry. Cuiyan Kezhen is the exact chamber speaker who asks a monk why Luzu faced the wall when a monk came to inquire; Luzu is the embedded subject of Cuiyan's question, not the speaker of this headword-bearing turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 達磨九年面壁鬼魅之由。二祖立雪求心翻成不肖。汝等諸人到這裏如何吐露。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 續傳燈錄. Full six-rung exact-turn review identifies Bailu Xianrui as the exact headword-bearing speaker, author, or grammatical actor for this occurrence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 達磨大師自梁涉魏至洛陽少林面壁而坐經於九年方得二祖傳法。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 禪宗頌古聯珠通集. Full six-rung exact-turn review identifies Bodhidharma as the exact headword-bearing speaker, author, or grammatical actor for this occurrence.
